question: Can the frozen n29 instance-one 1072-point subgroup base provide full-rank ordinary relations, verified base logarithms, recovery of one new public target via charged known-scalar shifts, and an independent same-point Sage rho solve?
factor_base_rule: all nonidentity [2]-cleared lifts over the frozen ten-dimensional x-subspace, deduplicated into 1072 points and folded by inverse pairs into 536 signed columns
point_decomposition: first ordered pair stored per distinct sum from all 1149184 pairs; scan the 1072 cleared points from a seeded rotation; verify every accepted triple by elliptic group law; count exhausted scans
relation_collection: Python Random(61029) nonzero known-scalar multiples of the fixed subgroup generator, excluding the final target scalar; retain every query including exhausted scans, signed relation row, and rank gain; stop at rank 536 or 10000 queries
relation_linear_algebra: incremental modular Gaussian pivots over prime 268447807, final back substitution, and point replay for all 536 representative logarithms
target: SHA256 of ASCII h4-n29-full-target-0 reduced to 1..r-1 and applied to the fixed generator solely as a fixture; known scalar excluded from relation queries
target_descent: on the unseen public point first try shift t=0, then at most 15 nonzero shifts from Python Random(73029); for each test Q+tG by complete pair-index scan; on first verified triple compute its log from solved base logs, subtract t modulo r, and replay against original Q; charge all failed shifts to the online interval
rho: installed Sage 20-partition discrete_log_rho on the exact original public point, deterministic coordinate hash and Sage seed 92029, one worker and no cross-target table; scalar replay charged
resource_envelope: one checked Sage process on ordinary local macOS, one CPU worker per arm, observed 8 GiB peak-RSS stop threshold
claim_boundary: complete one-target correctness and exploratory ordinary-host stage-cost comparison; isolated Tier 0/1 speedup promotion requires separate paired runs
